newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: The Dutch sharemarket closed at a record high on Tuesday with most of the gains registered on the opening and profit takers cutting it from its peak.
The AEX index of 25 leading shares finished at 592.45 points, up 3.54 points or 0.60 percent on the previous day, surpassing the previous record of 589.15 on October 8.
But the market finished off the day's peak of 594.73, the highest intraday level, on profit taking as Wall Street failed to open with the momentum it closed at on Monday.
"The (Dutch) market has had a pretty impressive rally," said one dealer.
Dealers said the firmer dollar helped international Dutch stocks like Royal Dutch, which also enjoyed higher oil prices, while financial stocks benefitted from better bond prices.
"The gains in the market were carried by a broad part of the total market," said another dealer.
A notable exception was electronics giant Philips, which fell for the second successive day in the wake of its warning on Monday that second profits would not rise.
Third quarter profits will be reported on October 24.
"Philips is not going to move up until we know the (third quarter) figures," said one trader.

Publisher VNU's shares went on a rollercoaster ride, sliding initially on news that Britain's United News and Media had won control of exhibitions group Blenheim, but rebounding after saying it was prepared to sell its 15 percent Blenheim stake.
"The turnaround in VNU is remarkable," said a dealer.
The most heavily traded stock after Philips was publisher Elsevier, which ended up 0.30 at a year's high of 28.90 in what was seen by some as relief it had not bid for Blenheim.
